static.title: The rotating disk
static.note: Two measurements. The Oort constants A and B from the proper motions of 1,570 Gaia stars, and the Milky Way’s circular speed against radius from Bhattacharjee et al. 2014 (the set for R0 = 8.3 kpc and V0 = 244 km/s), against a model of bulge, disk and halo.

samples.value: Measured: Gaia DR3 proper motions, fitted for A, B and the Sun’s motion together

The fit
samples.value: weights each star by 1 ÷ parallax², because the nearest stars scatter most in these units

samples.label: What this is
samples.value: Measured: published rotation-curve points, three sets cited in the data package (this is the R0 = 8.3 kpc set). The curves are a model.

samples.label: At 8.3 kpc
samples.value: model 231 km/s: stars and gas 231, halo 0

samples.label: The model
samples.value: A bulge fixed at 1.5 × 10¹⁰ M☉, an exponential disk, and a halo of constant speed far out. Errors are floored at 3 km/s. The disk is bounded at 8 × 10¹⁰ M☉ in the fits, since a disk with no bound can fit the curve alone and explain nothing.

static.note: Dos mediciones. Las constantes de Oort A y B a partir de los movimientos propios de 1.570 estrellas de Gaia, y la rapidez circular de la Vía Láctea según el radio, de Bhattacharjee et al. 2014 (el conjunto de R0 = 8,3 kpc y V0 = 244 km/s), frente a un modelo de bulbo, disco y halo.

samples.label: El modelo

static.title: Cluster membership by motion
static.note: The 993 Gaia DR3 stars brighter than G = 17.5 within 14 arcminutes of the open cluster NGC 2420. A cluster and a field are fitted together; each star gets a probability of belonging to the cluster, not a label.

samples.label: What this is
samples.value: Measured: Gaia DR3 astrometry and photometry (ESA/Gaia/DPAC). The membership is a model fit.

Distance from that parallax
samples.value: 2.60 kpc, as 1 ÷ parallax, with no zero-point correction (about 0.02 mas) and no check against another method

samples.label: The fit
samples.value: A narrow Gaussian for the cluster and a broad one for the field, fitted together by expectation-maximization from fixed starting values; each star’s own errors widen both.
